The author is once again stressing the continuity of the community’s worship arrangements. He is making clear that the men in this important role at the temple were **Levites**, not men without that lineage whom the governor may have appointed. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [these four men who served in the important office of chiefs of the gatekeepers were Levites]
הֵ֗מָּה אַרְבַּ֨עַת֙ גִּבֹּרֵ֣י הַ⁠שֹּׁעֲרִ֔ים הֵ֖ם הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֑ם

The author says **they** twice to emphasize that these **chiefs of the gatekeepers** had the necessary lineage as **Levites**. It might seem that repeating these pronouns would be to express extra information that would not be natural in your language. If so, you can convey the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [the four chiefs of the gatekeepers were genuine Levites]

If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [it was their responsibility to guard the temple area]

The author assumes that readers will understand that by **the opening**, he means the opening of the gates to the temple courtyard. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [responsible for opening the courtyard gates]

The author is using this common expression of his culture to mean “every morning.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. The author assumes that readers will understand that by **the chambers**, he means the chambers or rooms that adjoined the temple. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [who stayed in the temple chambers]

The author is using the two main components of time, day and night, to mean all of time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [constantly]

nt: The pronoun **they** does not refer to the Levites whom the author has been discussing. Instead, it refers to some members of the tribe of Benjamin.
